newsitem.title: USA: Incyte sees $38 mln in 1996 revenues.
newsitem.headline: Incyte sees $38 mln in 1996 revenues.

text.p: Incyte Pharmaceuticals Inc should report 1996 revenues of about $38 million, up from $12.2 million in 1995, President and Chief Executive Officer Roy Whitfield said.
He added that the company already has $65 million guaranteed in 1997 revenues. That amount does not include licensing fees on intellectual property, or new subscribers.
Whitfield, who spoke at the Hambrecht and Quist Healthcare Conference here, said revenues have reached the point where they are sufficient to fund the company's R&D.
Incyte, which develops genomic database products for gene mapping and gene sequencing, also expects to bring two new related products into development in 1997, Whitfield said.

The company Monday announced a licensing agreement with Genentech, which became its 12th subscriber. Drug companies use Incyte's genomics high-throughput sequencing products for drug discovery and development. Its gene sequencing technology has been doubling its capability about ever six months, Whitfield said.
Unlike initial work in gene identification, which located one gene at a time, the new technologies enable researchers to study thousands of genes at the same time.

"The old system of one gene at a time was not cutting it," Whitfield said. "The technology we have now makes it possible to pick apart complex disease systems in a way that's never before been possible."
Citing a universal need for such technology by pharmaceutical and biotech companies, Whitfield said: "We feel we have a unique opportunity to create an industry standard platform."
